findings.statement: Before buying, the buyer asked specifically about box condition and said it was most of what they were paying for; the seller answered that the sets had been stored in a cupboard since new and the boxes were fine.
The listing described four retired sets as used, like new, with boxes in good condition, at a price of 200.

The parcel was handed to the carrier on 26 August and delivered on 28 August with no exception or damage event recorded along the way; carrier records show movement only and say nothing about condition.
The buyer reported a badly crushed, split corner on one box the same day the parcel was delivered.
The photograph of the item shows a single London Architecture box with a crushed and torn upper corner and some scuffing along the edges; the rest of the box and its printing appear intact.
The seller maintains the sets were in good condition when sent and were packed carefully, but no picture of the packing or the outer parcel has been provided by either side.
The buyer raised the problem immediately after the purchase money was released, well inside the allowed window.

provisional.reasoning: One of four boxes arrived with a crushed, split corner, which is not the condition promised before the sale. The damage is confined to a corner of a single box and does not affect the other three sets or the contents, so it reduces the value of about a quarter of the order rather than the whole of it. A fifteen per cent share of the money being held reflects that loss of value.

requests.what: One photograph of the outer shipping parcel exactly as it arrived, with the flaps open so the padding or filling inside it can be seen next to where the sets sat.
requests.whyItMatters: The two of you agree the box has a crushed corner but not on how it got that way. The state of the outer parcel and what was packed around the sets is the one thing that shows whether the corner took a knock during the journey or was already like that when it was sent. Nobody has pictured the outer parcel yet, and it is the only item that speaks to the journey itself.

wouldChange.answer: The outer parcel is visibly crushed or punctured near the matching corner and there is little or no padding around the sets
wouldChange.implies: The damage happened in transit because the sets were not protected well enough, which is the sender's responsibility

wouldChange.answer: The outer parcel is undamaged and the sets were well padded
wouldChange.implies: The corner damage most likely predated shipping, so the description given before the sale was inaccurate

wouldChange.answer: The outer parcel shows heavy impact damage despite generous padding around the sets
wouldChange.implies: The sender packed properly and the harm was done by rough handling in transit, which neither party controlled

wouldChange.answer: No such photograph can be produced because the outer parcel was discarded
wouldChange.implies: The cause stays unresolved and the split rests on the size of the shortfall against what was promised
